title: Colonialism Phase Of Free Trade
definition: The second phase of British colonialism in India (approx. 1813 to 1858), characterized by the transformation of India into a consumer of British manufactured goods and a supplier of raw materials, driven by the industrial bourgeoisie in Britain.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Modern Indian History (GS-1) and Economy/Post-Independence (GS-3). Tests the structural shift from mercantile loot to industrial-capitalist exploitation, deindustrialization, commercialization of agriculture, and drain of wealth.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Colonialism Phase Of Free Trade.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
